A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same visual-grounding reliability framework for sign language translation. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination-detection and regression experiments on PHOENIX-2014T and CSL-Daily, alongside transfer, perturbation, pooling, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main comparisons in Tables 1–2 and supplementary results and examples in Appendices G–H.

M1.justification: The clean, no-video, and mismatched-video passes, reliability signals, fusion, pooling, and calibration remain unchanged. Added explanations of normalization and pooling clarify existing operations; quantile scaling was already documented in v1's Algorithm 1 and Appendix F.1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PHOENIX-2014T and CSL-Daily, covering German and Chinese sign language translation. Cross-dataset/model transfer, visual degradation, and adversarial-prefix scenarios are retained without new coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Grounding, META, confidence, perplexity, and token entropy, evaluated using SpaMo and TwoStream-SLT. Comparator membership in Table 1 and the supplementary comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F.2 removes the optional Chinese spaCy/POS-filtering pathway from the stated CHAIR preprocessing, retaining jieba segmentation, normalization, and stopword filtering. This narrowly revises the reported preprocessing options; it does not establish that preprocessing actually changed or experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix G retains the same visual-degradation tests, feature-weight analyses, pooling comparisons, and raw-probability interaction analysis. Appendix H retains the same translation-error and prompt-injection cases.

E5.justification: Tables 3–4 describe their values as means over runs in both versions. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain their numerical values and qualitative examples, and the plotted results are unchanged. For example, Grounding on CSL GF remains at 0.951 AUC, 0.998 AP, and 0.970 accuracy in Table 1. Figure 6 changes labels rather than results.

T1.justification: The mathematical operations and Appendix C's assumptions, proposition, proof, and continuous variant are retained. Main-text equations receive numbers and explanatory prose; the proposition's equation changes from (1) to (6), without changing its mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty, grounding, complementarity, transfer, and gloss-free hallucination claims. Calling reliability a measure instead of a metric clarifies terminology without changing contribution scope.

C2.justification: The explanations involving language priors, weak visual use, transfer behavior, and non-monotonic reliability remain unchanged. The added introductory definition of hallucination makes explicit the content-token focus already reflected in v1's appendix discussion and CHAIR computation.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies the binary labels: CHAIR > 0 is hallucinated and the remaining samples are negative. It also explicitly describes learning reliability weights for detection and CHAIR prediction. These clarify existing experiments rather than establish new training procedures.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are unchanged, including the claimed first investigation of hallucination in SLT and the relationship to counterfactual and text-only detection approaches.

P1.justification: v2 adds brief definitions and notation explanations, clarifies the Section 3.4 heading, corrects author-name spelling and grammar, and smooths several experimental passages. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 corrects its title's grounded-region color from green to orange and changes the right-axis label from Grounding Probability to Grounding Measure. Equation numbering and local figure/table placement also change with text reflow; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity and reproducibility by specifying the binary CHAIR label in Section 4.1, explaining existing notation, correcting prose, and fixing Figure 6's labels. These resolve limited reporting ambiguities while leaving the method, theoretical support, and empirical evidence essentially unchanged.
